title: The Grid—What it is
slide_intent: Teach designers to derive a publication grid from the material it must carry. Fixed alignment points give readers continuity as text and pictures change.
strategic_value: NASA can organize diverse publications efficiently by settling margins, gutters and folios before placing individual elements.
demonstration: Three numbered stages move from an empty spread to a two-column grid and then to a populated spread. Red guides expose the underlying alignments.
practical_value: Start with the trim size and required content. Establish margins, columns, gutter and folio positions, then block in actual text, headings, captions and images.

content_islands.name: Purpose of a grid
content_islands.spec: Place the heading beside a short explanation in the top columns.

content_islands.name: Format and guides
content_islands.spec: Stack the blank spread and the spread with red guides. Pair each drawing with its numbered instruction at left.

content_islands.name: Populated spread
content_islands.spec: Keep the same spread size for the final stage. Lay text, headings and the image against the visible grid and indicate the outer folio position.
